title: Rotate with stack and index
starter:
%a = param 0 dtype=i32
%b = param 1 dtype=i32
%c = param 2 dtype=i32
%i = param 3 dtype=i32
# stack a, b, c; j = i + 1 (i32 add, so INT_MAX + 1 wraps); return the element at j mod 3, fixed into 0..2. i=2 gives a
%out = add %a 0
hints: `stack` turns your three scalars into one rank-1 value, and `index` reads one element back out.
The element after position `i` is at position `i + 1`, wrapped back into 0, 1, 2 with `mod`.

`mod` keeps the sign of the dividend, so `mod (i + 1) 3` is negative when `i + 1` is (try `i = -2`, and `i = INT_MAX`, where `i + 1` wraps to `INT_MIN`). Add 3 and take `mod 3` again to land in 0, 1, 2.
explain: The reference stacks `a b c`, computes `(i + 1) mod 3`, then adds 3 and takes `mod 3` again. C-style `mod` can return -1 or -2 when `i + 1` is negative (including when `i = INT_MAX` wraps to `INT_MIN`), and the second `mod` folds that back into `[0, 2]`, which is what the bounds-checked `index` needs.
